summary: Hydroxyethyl starch (HES) is a synthetic colloid used intravenously for the treatment of hypovolaemia when plasma-volume expansion is desired; it is not a substitute for blood or plasma. The 6% formulation is also used as an adjunct in leukapheresis to improve granulocyte yield. The usual volume-expansion dose is 500-1000 mL, with daily doses usually not exceeding about 1500 mL (~20 mL/kg) for a 70 kg adult. HES carries a BOXED WARNING: it increases mortality and the need for renal replacement therapy in critically ill adults (including those with sepsis) and is associated with excess bleeding in patients undergoing open-heart surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. It is therefore contraindicated in critically ill patients, in severe liver disease, in pre-existing coagulation/bleeding disorders, and in conditions of fluid overload. Renal function should be monitored for at least 90 days because renal injury can present late.
indications: Treatment of hypovolaemia when plasma-volume expansion is desired (not a substitute for blood or plasma)
Adjunct in leukapheresis to improve the harvesting and yield of granulocytes

dosage.d: Usually 500-1000 mL IV; doses >1500 mL/day (~20 mL/kg) for a 70 kg patient usually not required
dosage.t: Intravenous infusion only; rate and total dose depend on blood/plasma loss and haemoconcentration
dosage.n: Higher doses reported only in major postoperative/trauma blood loss

dosage.d: 250-700 mL of 6% HES with citrate, added at a ratio of 1:8 to 1:13 to venous whole blood
dosage.t: Aseptic addition to the input line of the centrifugation apparatus
dosage.n: Mix thoroughly with citrate for effective anticoagulation

admin: Administer by intravenous infusion only; inspect for particulate matter/discoloration and use only if clear with intact seals
Do not connect plastic containers in series (air-embolism risk); stop pump before the container empties
Avoid excessive pressure (>300 mmHg) on the container to prevent breakage
Discontinue at the first sign of renal injury or coagulopathy
Monitor renal function in hospitalised patients for at least 90 days, as renal replacement therapy has been reported up to 90 days after use
Avoid use as cardiac bypass pump prime or during/immediately after cardiopulmonary bypass (bleeding risk)
moa: Hydroxyethyl starch is a synthetic colloid prepared from amylopectin by hydroxyethyl substitution that retards enzymatic degradation and prolongs intravascular persistence. As a high-molecular-weight osmotically active polymer it raises plasma colloid oncotic pressure, drawing and holding fluid in the intravascular compartment and thereby expanding plasma volume. The degree and duration of expansion depend on the molecular weight and molar substitution. Larger HES molecules can impair coagulation (a von Willebrand-/Factor VIII-like effect and platelet dysfunction) and accumulate in tissues including the kidney, underlying its renal and bleeding toxicities.

absolute: Critically ill adults, including patients with sepsis (increased mortality and need for renal replacement therapy)
Conditions with potential volume overload (e.g. congestive heart failure, renal disease with anuria/oliguria not due to hypovolaemia)
relative: Cardiopulmonary bypass / open-heart surgery (bleeding risk - not recommended)
Elderly patients and those at risk of fluid overload
Subarachnoid haemorrhage with repeated dosing (bleeding risk)
monitor: Coagulation status and signs of bleeding

preg: There are limited data on HES use in pregnancy. Anaphylactoid reactions can be hazardous to both mother and fetus, and volume effects must be carefully judged. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and when the benefit outweighs the potential risk.
lact: It is not known whether hydroxyethyl starch is excreted in human milk. Caution should be exercised when it is administered to a breastfeeding woman.
renal: BOXED WARNING applies: HES increases the need for renal replacement therapy and can cause renal injury, which may present late. Avoid in patients with pre-existing renal dysfunction, discontinue at the first sign of renal injury, and continue to monitor renal function in hospitalised patients for at least 90 days. Contraindicated in renal disease with anuria/oliguria not related to hypovolaemia.
hepatic: Hydroxyethyl starch is contraindicated in patients with severe liver disease. Use with caution and monitor in any degree of hepatic impairment.

major: Concurrent anticoagulants/antiplatelet agents - additive bleeding risk through HES-induced coagulopathy
Other nephrotoxic drugs (e.g. aminoglycosides) - additive renal injury
moderate: Drugs causing fluid retention - additive volume overload
Other plasma expanders - cumulative volume/coagulation effects
minor: May interfere with cross-matching/blood typing if large volumes given
interactions.alcohol: Not relevant for acute IV use
interactions.diagnostics: Can falsely raise serum amylase; may prolong coagulation tests; large volumes can interfere with blood typing/cross-matching

common: Dilutional reductions in haematocrit and plasma proteins
serious: Increased mortality in critically ill/septic patients
Acute kidney injury / need for renal replacement therapy
Coagulopathy and clinically significant bleeding (von Willebrand-/Factor VIII-like syndrome)
rare: Tissue/organ accumulation of HES with long-term itching
emergency: Acute pulmonary oedema from volume overload

monitoring: Renal function at baseline and for at least 90 days after administration
Coagulation parameters and clinical signs of bleeding
Haemodynamic and fluid-balance status to avoid overload
counsel: This is a drip used to expand the blood volume in hospital, given and monitored by your medical team
It is not used in seriously ill or septic patients because it can harm the kidneys and increase the risk of death
Tell staff straight away if you feel breathless, develop a rash or itching, or notice unusual bruising or bleeding
Your kidney function may be checked for some weeks afterwards
Itching can sometimes persist for a while after treatment
pk: Plasma-volume expansion begins during the infusion
Maximal volume effect at the end of infusion
Intravascular persistence of hours (varies with molecular weight/substitution); smaller fragments cleared renally
Volume effect lasts several hours; tissue-stored fractions persist much longer
Store at 20-25 C; avoid excessive heat; protect from freezing; use only if clear
pearls: BOXED WARNING: increased mortality and renal replacement therapy in critically ill adults (incl. sepsis), and excess bleeding in open-heart/cardiopulmonary bypass surgery
Contraindicated in critically ill patients, sepsis, severe liver disease, bleeding/coagulation disorders and volume-overload states
Monitor renal function for at least 90 days - injury can present late; discontinue at first sign of renal injury or coagulopathy
Causes a von Willebrand-/Factor VIII-like coagulopathy with repeated dosing; not for use as bypass pump prime
Crystalloids are generally preferred for resuscitation; reserve HES for selected non-critically-ill volume expansion and leukapheresis
missed: Not applicable - hydroxyethyl starch is given only as a clinician-administered IV infusion for acute volume needs, not as scheduled self-administered doses.
overdose: Overdose (excessive infusion) causes circulatory volume overload with pulmonary oedema and heart failure, and worsening coagulopathy with bleeding. Stop the infusion immediately and treat supportively: oxygen, diuretics for overload, and correction of coagulopathy (consider replacement of Factor VIII/von Willebrand factor for severe deficiency). Monitor renal function, fluid balance and coagulation closely.
